behavior_constraints: All classification evaluations (binary and multi-class) emit confusion matrix as {"labels": [sorted unique class strings], "matrix": [[counts]]} where matrix[i][j] counts instances with actual=labels[i] predicted=labels[j].
For binary classification, labels are ["0","1"], with matrix[0][0]=TN, matrix[0][1]=FP, matrix[1][0]=FN, matrix[1][1]=TP; the flat {TP,FP,TN,FN} object is no longer produced.
mlpipe registry list returns a wrapped object {"models": [...], "count": N} where count equals the length of models, including {"models": [], "count": 0} when no models match filters.
mlpipe registry promote <name:version> <target_stage> accepts an optional --force flag.
Without --force, promotion is rejected when promotion rules fail (success=false with rule-failure message), unchanged from previous behavior.

With --force, promotion proceeds even when rules fail, outputting {"success": true, "message": "promoted to production (forced)", "previous_stage": ..., "new_stage": ..., "warnings": [<overridden rule descriptions>]}.
When --force is used and no rules fail, the warnings field is an empty array.
Warning strings describe overridden rules, e.g. "metric accuracy (0.7500) below threshold (0.9900)".
mlpipe validate never writes to stderr; all errors including file-not-found and JSON parse errors are reported via stdout JSON {"valid": false, "errors": ["..."]}.
entities.summary: This round introduces breaking output/behavior changes: uniform structured confusion matrix format, wrapped registry list output, --force flag for registry promote that overrides rule failures with warnings, and stdout-only validate error reporting.

instruction_head:
After internal review, we've decided to make several breaking changes to improve consistency and prepare for production deployment. These changes affect existing output formats and command behavior.

## 1. Confusion Matrix Output Format Change

The confusion matrix metric output format is changing for ALL classification evaluations, including binary classification.

**Previous behavior:** Binary classification returned a flat object `{"TP": n, "FP": n, "TN": n, "FN": n}`.

**New behavior:** ALL
